evals.prompt: 첨부한 IFC(9 MB) 를 열면 창이 벽에서 1 m 떠 있어. 고치고 테스트 남겨줘.
evals.expected_output: Finds the failing path first, writes a feature list of observable features (the window, its host wall, the placement chain, the producer and units) before reducing anything, and uses that list as the test's assertions.
assertions: Writes the feature list before cutting or editing the file.
States each feature as something the test will observe, with exact kinds and values.
Pins the test on the original outside the repo before reducing.

evals.prompt: The bug only shows when a block definition in this DWG is inserted more than once. Reduce the sample to a fixture.
evals.expected_output: Lists multiplicity as a feature (one definition with at least two inserts) and keeps it in the fixture, and the mutation check removes the second insert to show the test then fails.
assertions: Includes 'definition shared by at least two users' in the feature list.
Does not reduce to a single insert.
Mutation check covers the multiplicity feature.

evals.prompt: I wrote a loop that deletes chunks of the file while the test still fails. It got the file down to 3 KB. Done?
evals.expected_output: Checks that the predicate also requires the format's authoritative reader to open the candidate without new errors; otherwise the reduction may now hit a parse-error path, so re-check the verdict reason and the reader.
assertions: Requires the authoritative reader to open the candidate as part of the predicate.
Requires the same verdict for the same reason, not just pass or fail.
Does not accept the 3 KB file on the test result alone.

evals.prompt: 픽스처 만들었고 원본이랑 픽스처 둘 다 테스트 통과해. 커밋할게.
evals.expected_output: Before committing, alters or removes each listed feature in a scratch copy and confirms the test fails each time; a feature whose removal stays green means the test is fixed, not the fixture.
assertions: Runs a mutation check per listed feature.
Treats a green after removal as a test defect.
Reopens the final file with the authoritative reader.

evals.prompt: Turn this customer's .xlsx into a test fixture for the import bug.
evals.expected_output: Looks for the repository's test-data recipe, existing generators, sample policy and trusted reader first and follows them; when none exists it works ad hoc and writes down what worked where the repo keeps such notes.
assertions: Searches the repo for a test-data doc, repo skill or generator before cutting.
Follows a found recipe instead of inventing one.
Leaves a recipe or note behind when none existed.

evals.prompt: The bug is in how we read a CSV whose header has a duplicated column name. The sample is a 40 MB export. Add a test.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the lightest form: a few CSV lines built in test code (or a tiny generator), not a cut of the 40 MB export and not the original kept outside.
assertions: Uses built-in test data or a generator rather than committing a cut of the export.
Explains why the lighter form keeps every listed feature.
Does not reference the original by path in the test.

evals.prompt: 이 도면은 고객사 실제 현장 파일인데 잘라서 픽스처로 쓰려고 해. 레포에는 고객 데이터 관련 규칙이 없어.
evals.expected_output: Scrubs names, addresses, metadata, paths, thumbnails and real-world coordinates the feature list does not need, and asks the user once before committing a cut of the customer's file; notes forms 1 and 2 would need no such answer.
assertions: Scrubs content not in the feature list, moving coordinates to the origin unless georeferencing is a feature.
Asks the user once before committing a derived customer cut.
Does not ask when the fixture is built in test code or generated.

evals.prompt: Our load-time benchmark reads a 600 MB model from the shared drive. Should I reduce it to a fixture too?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the performance input whole and outside the repo; the test must state that it skips when the file is absent and its green elsewhere is not evidence.
assertions: Does not reduce a performance or corpus input.
Requires the test to say it skips when the file is absent.
Does not commit the large file.

evals.prompt: Fixture is ready at tests/fixtures/door-offset.ifc. The test opens C:/Users/me/samples/door-offset.ifc for comparison. Finish up.
evals.expected_output: Repoints the test to the repo-relative fixture path, removes the machine path, and writes provenance beside the fixture: feature list, source description plus content hash, form and why, and the regenerate or re-reduce command.
assertions: Removes every machine path from the test.
Records the source as a description and content hash, not a private path or customer name.
Leaves the regenerate or re-reduce command next to the fixture.
